Why multi-page is a different problem

An Evidence-Management Problem

What the document does to the model
Exceeds the context window total length outruns the backbone
Evidence sparse & scattered a few pages carry the answer
Structure spans pages hierarchy, cross-references, tables
Long document p1 … pN
What the system does back
Retrieve relevant pages rank and pass a compact subset
Compress / sample fit a fixed token budget
Preserve visual fidelity keep what text extraction loses
The system must decide what to retain, discard, retrieve, or acquire.
02 / 07·An Evidence-Management Problem
Multi-page multimodal representation

What Makes Multi-Page Hard?

Every evidence decision is enacted over a modality. Three axes, three sets of pressures.
Text§4.1
Reading everything is impossible; every fix is lossy somewhere.
Volume
length outruns the context
Continuity
paragraphs and tables break at page edges
Noise
OCR error accumulates across pages
Heterogeneity
text density varies page to page
Visual§4.2
Pixels keep what text extraction loses, but they cost tokens.
Resolution
cannot hold full fidelity at document length
Signal competition
text, figures and layout share one budget
Heterogeneity
visual complexity varies page to page
Structure§4.3
What turns isolated pages into one document.
Hierarchy
sections and reading order span the whole file
Cross-page references
“see Figure 3” points somewhere else
Spanning elements
tables and paragraphs continue across pages
Cross-cutting

Multi-hop reasoning: the answer is assembled from pages that are far apart, so no single page scores well on its own.

03 / 07·What Makes Multi-Page Hard?
§3 · Four architectural families

MP-VRDU Architecture Overview

evidence handled inside the backbone
the trend
outside it, orchestrated at inference
What to notice

Each family pushes evidence handling further out of the backbone, through compression, then retrieval, then iterative orchestration. None of them removes the bottleneck; each relocates it (the red note under every panel is that family's price).

04 / 07·MP-VRDU Architecture Overview
Current work · representation ladder

Accuracy vs. Evidence Richness

Rungs T text TL + layout TV + page image TLV all three V image only cost increases left to right
Pooled · all questions
By document domain · 7 domains
By evidence source · 5 sources
What to notice

Accuracy climbs with richness and peaks at TLV, 31.9 to 52.5, but the ladder is not monotonic: dropping text for the page image alone costs 6.9 points. Richer rungs also absorb parser quality, with the spread between parsers falling from 13.6 points at TL to 5.1 at TLV. The shape holds across every domain and evidence source; only the height moves.

Missing vs. Distracting Evidence

Reading the table · TLV column
Sufficiency

Losing evidence is unrecoverable

all gold pages43.6
drop one gold18.5
keep one gold12.8

Removing a single required page costs more than half the accuracy. No rung of the ladder recovers it: the model answers anyway.

Robustness · 1-gold pool

Distraction is mostly absorbed

no distractor64.6
+3 distractors63.1

But tolerance shrinks as more pages are required, so the risk is not distraction itself, it is distraction on top of multi-hop evidence.
